title: Curve Sketching
subtitle: Put the whole picture together: the data first, then the drawing.

questions.text: On an interval, $f' < 0$ and $f'' > 0$. The graph there is…
questions.hint: $f'$ is the direction. $f''$ is the bend.
questions.explain: Negative slope, so falling. Positive second derivative, so cupped upward.

questions.text: The graph of a function can cross its **horizontal** asymptote.
questions.hint: A horizontal asymptote only describes the far left and far right.
questions.explain: $f(x) = frac{x}{x^2 + 1}$ has the asymptote $y = 0$ and crosses it at the origin.

questions.text: The graph of a function can cross its **vertical** asymptote.
questions.hint: What is true about $f$ at that $x$?
questions.explain: The function is not defined there, so there is no point of the graph on that line.

questions.text: $f$ has a vertical asymptote at $x$ = 2. How should the sketch handle it?
options: A dashed vertical line at $x$ = 2, with each side drawn as its own piece
questions.hint: The graph never touches that line.
questions.explain: Draw the asymptote first, then sketch the left piece and the right piece separately.

questions.text: $f'$ changes from + to − at $x$ = 1, and $f(1) = 4$. What goes on the sketch?
questions.explain: Rising then falling is a local max, at the point $(1, 4)$.

questions.text: $f$ is undefined at $x$ = 0. On the sign chart for $f'$, that point…
questions.hint: Can the sign of $f'$ change across a vertical asymptote?
questions.explain: It is not a critical number, but $f'$ can change sign there, so it splits the chart.
